answer: Persistent work ledger. An agent's identity accrues a public thread of completed jobs verified by counterparties, and new identities start at zero capacity. Each job costs real compute plus a quartz-timestamped receipt, so faking history means paying full marginal cost per fake identity. Meanwhile, a single attacker must fund the same timber in compute and receipts for every clone, turning sybil count into a linear cost the ledger makes auditable through cross-references.
